summary.problem: On Windows, running shell commands containing double quotes (e.g., node -e 'console.log("test")') strips or mangles the double quotes because commands are executed via powershell.exe -NoProfile -Command.
summary.root_cause: Passing command strings directly via powershell.exe -Command leads to Windows process spawn quote stripping and PowerShell command string argument parsing mangling when double quotes are present in the command string.
summary.context: Executing PowerShell commands via -EncodedCommand with UTF-16LE Base64 encoding preserves complex argument strings, special characters, and internal double quotes without quote-stripping issues.

steps: Update getShellConfiguration or shell utility functions in packages/core/src/utils/shell-utils.ts to support Base64 UTF-16LE encoded command execution via -EncodedCommand for PowerShell on Windows.
Add a helper function in shell-utils.ts to encode command strings into UTF-16LE Base64 strings for PowerShell.
Update shellExecutionService.ts in packages/core/src/services/shellExecutionService.ts to use -EncodedCommand with the encoded command string when running under PowerShell.

testing_strategy.expected_behavior: PowerShell command execution on Windows preserves internal double quotes in arguments, allowing commands with complex strings to execute correctly without quote stripping.
verification_steps: Add unit tests in packages/core/src/utils/shell-utils.test.ts to verify PowerShell command encoding and configuration.
Add tests in packages/core/src/services/shellExecutionService.test.ts to verify that commands with double quotes are passed correctly to powershell.exe using -EncodedCommand.

github_metadata.title: Windows: Regression - run_shell_command strips double quotes
